newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram opposes state guarantees.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram opposes state guarantees.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Wednesday government guarantees for infrastructure projects were "anti-market" and should be avoided.

"I believe that guarantees are essentially anti-market. Guarantees could easily become a substitute for real sectoral policies of institutional reforms," Chidambaram said at the start of a two-day global infrastructure conference in Delhi.
India has offered counter-guarantees for three of its eight fast-track power projects including those by U.S. firms Enron and Cogentrix.

"We ought not to grant counter-guarantees. They may be necessary to kick-start infrastructure in crucial areas but in the long run it is better to leave these issues to the market," Chindambaram said.
"Risk unbundling and the assignment of risk is a much better alternative than state counter-guarantees," he said.
Bong-Suh Lee, Asian Development Bank's vice president (West), told reporters after the session, guarantees were good as a concept but had their limitations.
"I realise there is a problem in counter-guarantees. It is something we have to discuss...it's a relatively new issue," Lee said.
